DMV Practice Test  #16
										  					
  

50 Questions • Passing Score 44

questions.question: When driving on major highways, what should you do?

options.text: Be ready to react to road hazards.

questions.explanation: On highways, you need to stay alert and be ready to react to unexpected hazards. Move your eyes frequently to avoid highway hypnosis—don't stare at one spot for more than a few seconds.

questions.question: An oncoming car is on your left and a bicyclist is on your right. What should you do?

options.text: Let the car pass and then pass the bike.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let the car pass and then pass the bike.
questions.explanation: When facing multiple hazards, handle one at a time. Let the oncoming car pass first, then pass the bicyclist. Don't try to squeeze between both at the same time.

questions.question: You are stranded in a snowstorm. What should you do?

options.text: Get out of the car and go for help.
Lay down in your car and go to sleep.
Walk into the road and get the attention of other drivers.
Stay in the car. You are most likely to be found when you stay in your vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay in the car. You are most likely to be found when you stay in your vehicle.
questions.explanation: Stay in your car and wait for help. You are easier to find if you don't leave your vehicle. Walking around outside in a snowstorm is dangerous.

questions.question: You see a flashing yellow arrow at a traffic signal. What can you do?

options.text: Merge into a lane in the direction of the arrow.
Turn left after yielding to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.
Turn left because you have the right-of-way.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn left after yielding to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow arrow means you can turn left in that direction. However, oncoming traffic has a green light, so you must yield to them and to pedestrians.

questions.question: This road sign means:

options.text: Reduce your speed when pavement is wet.
The road ahead has a series of turns or curves.

questions.correctAnswerText: Reduce your speed when pavement is wet.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that the pavement is slippery when wet. In wet conditions, reduce your speed, avoid sudden braking or turns, and increase your distance from the car ahead.

questions.question: A steady yellow traffic signal means a ____ light will come next.
questions.explanation: A steady yellow light warns you that a steady red light is coming next.

questions.question: This sign means:
questions.explanation: This yellow warning sign tells drivers that lanes will shift. Follow the new lane path ahead.

questions.question: This sign shows one type of:
questions.explanation: This sign warns that a T intersection is ahead.

questions.question: How does alcohol affect your reflexes and judgment?

options.text: Less when you drink beer instead of wine.
Less when you drink wine instead of beer.
Most when you drink hard ciders and mixed drinks.
It depends on the amount of alcohol in your blood.

questions.correctAnswerText: It depends on the amount of alcohol in your blood.
questions.explanation: Any type of alcohol hurts your reflexes and judgment. The type of drink doesn't matter—only how much alcohol is in your bloodstream.

questions.question: This road sign means:
questions.explanation: This sign means U-turns are not allowed at this location.

questions.question: At dusk or on overcast days, you should:

options.text: Drive with your four-way flashers on.
Drive with your parking lights on.

questions.explanation: You must turn on your headlights at dusk and on overcast days. Use low beams when you are within 1,000 feet of an oncoming vehicle or within 500 feet of a vehicle ahead of you. Always use low beams in bad weather.

questions.question: This sign means:
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. They alert drivers to upcoming road conditions and hazards. This sign warns about a steep hill ahead. Slow down to avoid brake damage or crashes.

questions.question: You are involved in an accident. You should:
questions.explanation: After an accident, stop your vehicle right away. Move it out of traffic if you can. Call the police and ask for an ambulance if needed. Do not move injured people unless necessary. Apply direct pressure to stop severe bleeding. Wait for emergency vehicles.

questions.question: At a light rail intersection, always:

options.text: Look both ways before crossing tracks.
Pay attention and obey all traffic signals.
Share the road with pedestrians and bicyclists.

questions.explanation: Never drive around lowered crossing gates. Look both ways before crossing train tracks. Obey all signs and traffic signals. Trains, cars, bicycles, and pedestrians all share the road.

questions.question: You may drive around the gates at a railroad crossing:

options.text: When the lights have stopped flashing.
When other drivers drive around the gates.

questions.explanation: You must stop at all railroad crossings when warning signals appear. These signals include flashing red lights, lowered gates, a flagperson, or a train horn. Never drive around a lowered gate.

questions.question: When sharing the road with a truck, it is important to remember that trucks generally:

options.text: Require longer distances to stop than smaller vehicles do.
Require less time to pass on a downgrade than smaller vehicles do.
Require a smaller turning radius than smaller vehicles do.
Require less time to pass on an incline than smaller vehicles do.

questions.correctAnswerText: Require longer distances to stop than smaller vehicles do.
questions.explanation: Trucks need longer distances to stop because of their size.

questions.question: Motorcycles are entitled to:

options.text: The same full lane width as other motor vehicles.
Half the width of a lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: The same full lane width as other motor vehicles.
questions.explanation: Motorcyclists must use the lane correctly. Motorcycles are entitled to the same full lane width as all other vehicles.

questions.question: You must stop for a school bus:

options.text: That is parked on the shoulder with no one in it.
When it approaches you, even if its lights are not flashing.
If you are both on a two-lane highway and its red lights are flashing.
Whenever the driver waves at you.

questions.correctAnswerText: If you are both on a two-lane highway and its red lights are flashing.
questions.explanation: Stop when you see a school bus with flashing red lights while it is picking up or dropping off children. On a two-lane road, traffic in both directions must stop and stay stopped while the red lights are flashing and the stop arm is extended.

questions.question: You may drive across a dashed white line:

options.text: When it is safe to change lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: When it is safe to change lanes.
questions.explanation: Dashed white lines separate lanes moving in the same direction. You may cross dashed lines to change lanes or pass if it is safe.

questions.question: From the center lane, which maneuver(s) can you perform?
questions.explanation: This lane is reserved only for left turns from either direction. You cannot use it for passing or driving straight.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are diamond-shaped with black markings on a yellow background. They warn drivers about hazards ahead. This sign tells you a steep hill is coming. Slow down and be ready to adjust your speed.

questions.question: When dealing with pedestrians, a driver must:

options.text: Make sure the pedestrian sees your vehicle.
Always yield the right-of-way, even if the pedestrian is wrong.
Yield only when the pedestrian has the legal right-of-way.
Slow down and honk near a crosswalk.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always yield the right-of-way, even if the pedestrian is wrong.
questions.explanation: You must do everything possible to avoid hitting a pedestrian, no matter the situation. It is your job to watch for pedestrians and yield to them, even if they are crossing illegally.

questions.question: On a vertical traffic light, which color is on top, middle, and bottom?
questions.explanation: On vertical traffic lights, red is always on top and green is always on bottom. On horizontal lights, red is always on the left and green is always on the right.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are diamond-shaped with black markings on a yellow background. They warn drivers about hazards ahead. This sign means the divided highway will end soon.

questions.question: A driver is turning left and a pedestrian is crossing without a traffic light. Who must yield?
questions.explanation: Drivers must yield to pedestrians crossing at any intersection without a traffic light, whether or not there is a marked crosswalk.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: You must come to a complete stop.
Drive with caution and be ready to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must come to a complete stop.
questions.explanation: An eight-sided sign always means stop. You must come to a complete stop. Wait for vehicles or pedestrians to clear before you go.

questions.question: The light is green and you want to turn left, but traffic is heavy. What should you do?

options.text: Wait at the crosswalk for traffic to clear.
Wait in the center of the intersection for traffic to clear.
Go because you have a green light.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait in the center of the intersection for traffic to clear.
questions.explanation: If the light is green, you may enter the intersection to prepare for your left turn. Wait in the center for oncoming traffic to pass before you turn.

questions.question: You must not drive faster than:

options.text: A speed that is reasonable and safe.
A speed that is safe for current conditions.

questions.explanation: You must drive at a reasonable and safe speed. Consider the area, traffic, pedestrians, weather, road condition, and lighting. You must follow all speed limits.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Eight-sided signs mean stop. You must stop and give the right-of-way to others at the intersection. You may go when it is safe.

questions.question: There is a solid yellow line and a broken yellow line. The broken line is next to your lane. When can you pass?
questions.explanation: When the broken yellow line is on your side, you may cross it to pass if there is no oncoming traffic.

questions.question: What does a solid yellow line on your side of the centerline mean?
questions.explanation: A solid yellow line on your side means you cannot pass other vehicles.

questions.question: What can happen if a person drives much slower than the speed limit?

options.text: They are a very safe driver.
They should not let following cars pass.
They may create a dangerous driving environment.

questions.correctAnswerText: They may create a dangerous driving environment.
questions.explanation: Driving much slower than other traffic can be unsafe. On a two-lane road, you must pull over and let cars behind you pass if traffic backs up. Only drive slowly when weather or road conditions require it.

questions.question: What should you do when approaching an uncontrolled intersection?

options.text: Stop, check all directions, and proceed.

questions.explanation: At an intersection with no stop sign or traffic signal, yield to cars coming from the right. Always be ready to yield by easing off the gas, covering the brake, and looking left, right, and left again.

questions.question: You are driving on a highway with two solid yellow lines. When can you cross these lines?

options.text: Only to turn left into an alley, private road, or driveway.
To pass other vehicles if there is no oncoming traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Only to turn left into an alley, private road, or driveway.
questions.explanation: Double solid yellow lines mean no passing from either direction. You can only cross them to turn left into an alley, private road, or driveway.

questions.question: What must you do if a transit vehicle signals to re-enter the roadway after stopping?

options.text: Honk to let them know you're there.

questions.explanation: You must yield to a transit vehicle signaling to enter traffic after loading or unloading passengers. Change lanes, slow down, or stop if needed.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign tells you that the right lane will end.

questions.question: What does a flashing red light on a traffic signal mean?

options.text: It means the same as a stop sign.
You do not have to stop completely.

questions.correctAnswerText: It means the same as a stop sign.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light works like a stop sign. Stop completely, check for traffic and pedestrians, and proceed only when safe.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign tells drivers turning left on a green light to yield to oncoming traffic and turn only when safe.

questions.question: When do roads become very slippery?

options.text: After it has been raining for an hour or more.
During the first 10 to 15 minutes of a rainstorm.
Right after the rain has stopped.

questions.correctAnswerText: During the first 10 to 15 minutes of a rainstorm.
questions.explanation: During the first 10 to 15 minutes of rain, oil in the asphalt rises to the road surface, making it slippery. Hot weather makes this worse.

questions.question: What usually causes hydroplaning?
questions.explanation: At high speeds, your tires cannot push water off the road. They lose grip and slide on the water. This is hydroplaning.

questions.question: When a traffic signal light turns green, what should you do?

options.text: Speed up as fast as you can.
Wait for another driver to wave you on.

questions.explanation: A green light means you can go. But first, you must let pedestrians and other traffic clear the intersection.

questions.question: Turning your head to check your blind spot before changing lanes or merging is:

options.text: Not needed if you use your rearview mirror.

questions.explanation: Always check your blind spot by looking over your shoulder before changing lanes. Do not rely on mirrors alone.

questions.question: When driving on slippery roads, you should:

options.text: Drive normally like you would on dry roads.

questions.explanation: On slippery roads, increase the space between you and the car ahead. Your vehicle will need more time to stop.

questions.question: Work zone signs mean:

options.text: You must stop and back up right away.
Road conditions are not ideal for driving.
Drive faster to get through the work zone.

questions.correctAnswerText: Road conditions are not ideal for driving.
questions.explanation: Work zone signs are orange. They tell you that work is happening on or near the road. Be extra careful when you see these signs.

questions.question: A flashing red traffic signal works the same as:
questions.explanation: At a flashing red signal, you must stop and let all other traffic pass before you go.

questions.question: This road sign means:
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that a four-way intersection is coming.

questions.question: This sign means:
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. They alert you to upcoming road conditions and hazards. This sign tells you the shoulder is lower than the paved road.

questions.question: This road sign means:

options.text: You must turn right or left.
A road is joining from the right.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must turn right or left.
questions.explanation: This sign shows a Y intersection ahead. You must choose to go right or left.

questions.question: When you want to make a right turn, your car should be:

options.text: In the center of the street.
On the left side of the street.
On the right side of the street.
Past the center of the intersection when you start to turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: On the right side of the street.
questions.explanation: Position your car as far right as possible before turning right. Do not cut across other lanes.

questions.question: At an intersection with no signs or signals, you arrive at the same time as a vehicle to your right. What should you do?

options.text: Speed up and go through the intersection.
Slow down and let the vehicle on your right go first.
Drive through and make the other vehicle stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and let the vehicle on your right go first.
questions.explanation: When two vehicles arrive at the same time with no signals or signs, the vehicle on the right has the right-of-way. Let it pass before you proceed.
